DOCUMENT 1 — Email from deal counsel (Jenna Park, Wilson & Cross) re Project Falcon diligence, dated August 11, 2026:

Counsel — quick update on Falcon. Data room round two is open. Three things surfaced this week. First, the target's consumer app has been collecting precise geolocation since 2023 without a separate consent flow — their privacy policy mentions "location information" generically. Roughly 40% of their MAU is in California and another 15% in the EU. Second, their DPO resigned in June and hasn't been replaced; the role is being covered informally by the GC. Third, they signed an enterprise deal with a hospital system in Q1 that includes a BAA, but nobody on their side can locate an executed copy — only a draft. Separately, FYI, their office lease in Austin expires in December and they're planning to go remote-first; facilities is handling. Also the target's marketing team wants an intro call about co-branding after close — I said we'd circle back post-signing. Buyer's insurance broker asked whether we want a separate cyber policy or to extend the rep & warranty policy to cover privacy remediation; they need an answer by August 22. — Jenna

DOCUMENT 2 — Internal memo from associate (Dan Meyer) re Project Falcon target data practices, dated August 12, 2026:

Summary of target's data practices based on data room review and management calls. The target operates a consumer fitness app (4.2M MAU) and an enterprise wellness platform. Consumer side: collects health metrics (heart rate, sleep, workouts), precise geolocation (running routes), and connects to Apple Health / Google Fit. Retention is indefinite — no deletion schedule found in the data room. They use three ad SDKs in the free tier of the app; one of them (VectorPulse) receives session-level health-adjacent events (workout start/stop, duration). No data processing agreement with VectorPulse was located, only click-through terms. Enterprise side: employers get aggregated wellness dashboards; contracts reviewed so far (14 of 61) contain customary DPAs with SCCs for EU transfers. Engineering confirmed on Tuesday's call that the consumer database and enterprise database share a common user table where an employee also uses the consumer app. Management says a migration to separate them was "80% scoped" in 2025 but deprioritized. The target's bug bounty program paid out twice in 2025 for auth-bypass findings; both patched within a week per the changelog. Office snack vendor contract auto-renews in September.
